_note: Each segment is one narration line plus the footage it plays over. `src` is 'app' (the screen recording, with a start time in seconds) or 'slide' (a rendered deck slide by number). Audio duration drives the cut length, so the voice never runs past its picture.

segments.text: TrustPay. A payment system for work where neither side wants to go first.
It opens on the promise the whole product has to keep. Your money, protected.
You create an account, and a wallet is opened for you automatically.
This is running against a live server. Real accounts, a real database, real rules.

Here is the idea. A bank transfer moves money and carries none of the conditions around it. No milestone. No definition of done. No approval step. TrustPay puts those conditions inside the payment. Money enters a protected state and stays there until the work is approved.
Every account gets a Trust Score.
Seventy-two out of a hundred, medium risk. But a score you cannot question is just a number, so every point is accounted for.
Normal activity, consistent amounts, no cancellations. Against that: vague milestone criteria, little history, a very new account.
It even says its own confidence is limited. The score is there to inform you. It never blocks a payment on its own.
A project sets out the work. You define each milestone, what it covers, and what counts as finished.
That completion criteria field is deliberate. Vague conditions are the most common cause of disputes.
The wallet separates money into what is available, what is protected, and what is settling.
Balances stay hidden until you unlock them with a fingerprint.

Withdrawals go to a bank account or a UPI ID. The app checks the IFSC against the live bank registry, and it will not call an account verified until a payment provider has confirmed it belongs to you.
There is an assistant for the questions people actually ask.
Where is my payment? It answers from your own data, and it is labelled as AI generated, because a decision about money should not come from a model.
A traditional payment is send, then receive. TrustPay is agree, define, protect, work, verify, release. That chain is the product.
